inputs.desc: Enzyme used for chromatin digestion (HindIII, DpnII, MboI, or Arima for multiple enzymes)

outputs.name: contact-matrix
outputs.desc: Normalized chromatin interaction matrix at multiple resolutions (1kb, 5kb, 25kb, 100kb, 1Mb)

outputs.name: three-d-features
outputs.desc: TAD boundaries, A/B compartments, and chromatin loops with statistical confidence

process: Process Hi-C reads with HiC-Pro: align each mate independently to the reference (Hi-C mates map to different genomic locations due to ligation), assign read pairs to restriction fragments, filter invalid pairs (dangling ends, self-circles, PCR duplicates), and build the contact matrix. Valid interaction rate should be 40-60% of total read pairs for a good library.

Generate contact matrices at multiple resolutions using cooler: 1kb (requires >1 billion valid contacts), 5kb, 25kb (standard for TAD calling), 100kb, and 1Mb (for compartment analysis). Normalize with ICE (iterative correction and eigenvector decomposition) or KR (Knight-Ruiz) balancing to correct for biases from GC content, mappability, and restriction fragment length.

Call A/B compartments at 100kb or 1Mb resolution: compute the correlation matrix from the normalized contact matrix, then extract the first eigenvector (PC1) using cooltools eigs-cis. PC1 values partition the genome into A compartment (positive: gene-dense, GC-rich, active chromatin, early replicating) and B compartment (negative: gene-poor, AT-rich, repressive marks, late replicating). Correlate PC1 with GC content to orient the sign correctly.

Call TADs at 25kb or 40kb resolution: use insulation score method (cooltools insulation --window-sizes 500000). Insulation score measures the aggregate interaction frequency across each genomic position. TAD boundaries are local minima in the insulation score profile. Alternative methods: TopDom, HiCExplorer hicFindTADs. TAD boundaries are enriched for CTCF binding sites and cohesin.

Detect chromatin loops with HiCCUPS (from Juicer) or cooltools dots. Loops appear as focal enrichments (bright spots) in the contact matrix, representing stable interactions between specific loci (e.g., enhancer-promoter pairs). Loop detection requires high resolution (5-10kb) and deep sequencing (>1 billion valid contacts for genome-wide detection).

Integrate Hi-C features with other data: overlay TAD boundaries with CTCF ChIP-seq peaks (boundaries should be enriched for convergent CTCF motifs), compare compartment calls with histone marks (A compartment with H3K27ac, B compartment with H3K27me3 or H3K9me3), and intersect loops with enhancer-promoter predictions from H3K27ac and gene expression data.

description: Run a clinical-grade genomic analysis pipeline from panel design through variant interpretation and pharmacogenomics, meeting CAP/CLIA accreditation standards.

steps.description: Design and validate a clinical sequencing panel for diagnostic use. Panel design specifies target genes, capture probes, and performance criteria. Validation establishes analytical sensitivity, specificity, reproducibility, and reportable range using reference materials (Genome in a Bottle, Horizon Discovery controls). Meeting CAP/CLIA requirements for laboratory-developed tests.

inputs.name: clinical-indication
inputs.desc: Disease area and gene list for the diagnostic panel

inputs.name: reference-materials
inputs.desc: Well-characterized samples with known variants for validation (NA12878/HG001, NA24385/HG002)

outputs.name: validated-panel-spec
outputs.desc: Panel design with target regions, expected coverage, and validated performance metrics

outputs.name: validation-report
outputs.desc: Analytical validation data: sensitivity, specificity, reproducibility, and limitations

process: Define target regions: gene list from clinical guidelines (e.g., NCCN for cancer predisposition, ACMG SF v3.2 for incidental findings). Include coding exons plus 20bp flanking intronic sequence (covers canonical splice sites). For known pathogenic deep intronic variants, add those specific positions. Total target size determines sequencing cost and required depth.

Select capture method: hybridization capture (Twist, IDT, Agilent) for panels > 50 genes or amplicon-based (QIAseq, AmpliSeq) for small focused panels (< 50 genes). Hybridization capture provides more uniform coverage and better CNV detection. Amplicon has lower input DNA requirements (10ng vs 200ng).

Define coverage requirements: minimum 250x mean coverage for germline, 500x for somatic (to detect low allele fractions). At least 95% of target bases must reach 20x (germline) or 100x (somatic). Regions consistently below threshold are excluded from the reportable range and listed as limitations.

Validate analytical performance: run at least 5 replicates of reference samples with known variants (Genome in a Bottle truth set for NA12878). Calculate sensitivity (true positives / (true positives + false negatives)) targeting >99% for SNVs, >95% for indels. Specificity (true negatives / (true negatives + false positives)) targeting >99.9%. Include intra-run and inter-run reproducibility.

Establish limit of detection for somatic panels: serial dilutions of a tumor cell line into normal DNA at 50%, 25%, 10%, 5%, 2.5% variant allele fractions. Determine the minimum allele fraction detected at 95% sensitivity for each variant type.

Document the validation in a format meeting CAP checklist requirements: test description, specimen types, analytical performance characteristics, reference range, reportable range, limitations (regions with insufficient coverage, variant types not detected), and validation study data.

steps.description: Classify variants according to ACMG/AMP guidelines (5-tier system: pathogenic, likely pathogenic, variant of uncertain significance, likely benign, benign) using a structured evidence framework. Each evidence criterion (population frequency, computational predictions, functional data, segregation, de novo status) contributes weighted evidence toward pathogenicity or benignity. ClinGen expert panels provide gene-specific rule modifications.

inputs.name: annotated-variants
inputs.desc: Variants annotated with population frequency, computational predictions, and ClinVar status

inputs.name: clinical-phenotype
inputs.desc: Patient phenotype, family history, and inheritance pattern

outputs.name: classified-variants
outputs.desc: Each variant classified as P/LP/VUS/LB/B with evidence criteria applied

outputs.name: clinical-report-draft
outputs.desc: Structured report with variant table, interpretation, methodology, and limitations

process: Apply ACMG/AMP evidence criteria systematically for each variant. Population data: BA1 (allele frequency > 5% in any population, standalone benign), BS1 (frequency greater than expected for disorder), PM2 (absent or extremely low frequency in gnomAD: use the filtering allele frequency framework from Whiffin et al. to set gene-specific thresholds rather than a fixed cutoff).

Computational evidence: PP3 (multiple computational tools predict damaging: REVEL > 0.7, CADD > 25, SpliceAI > 0.5 for splice variants), BP4 (tools predict benign: REVEL < 0.15). Use REVEL as the primary missense predictor (outperforms individual tools). For splice variants, SpliceAI delta scores > 0.2 indicate potential splicing impact, > 0.5 is strong evidence.

Functional evidence: PS3 (well-established functional study shows damaging effect: protein stability, enzyme activity, transport, splicing assay), BS3 (functional study shows no damaging effect). Evaluate the assay: is it validated, does it measure the relevant protein function, is the effect size clinically meaningful? ClinGen Sequence Variant Interpretation working group provides functional assay evaluation criteria.

Segregation and de novo evidence: PS2 (de novo, confirmed by maternity and paternity testing: strong pathogenic), PM6 (assumed de novo without parental confirmation: moderate), PP1 (co-segregation with disease in multiple affected family members: supporting to strong depending on LOD score). For recessive conditions, PM3 (variant detected in trans with a known pathogenic variant).

Combine evidence following ACMG/AMP combining rules: pathogenic requires (PVS1 + >= 1 moderate) or (>= 2 strong) or (1 strong + >= 2 moderate/supporting) etc. Check ClinGen gene-specific recommendations that modify default criteria (e.g., specific functional domains where missense variants are pathogenic, adjusted PP3 thresholds).

Handle VUS appropriately: do not report VUS as causative. Provide a clear statement that VUS may be reclassified as more evidence becomes available. Recommend periodic reassessment. For clinical decision-making, VUS should not drive treatment changes but may inform surveillance decisions in context.

steps.description: Genotype pharmacogenes, assign star alleles and metabolizer phenotypes, and report drug-gene interactions following CPIC (Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium) guidelines. Pharmacogenomics translates genetic variation in drug-metabolizing enzymes, transporters, and targets into actionable prescribing recommendations.

inputs.name: sequencing-data
inputs.desc: Targeted sequencing or WGS data covering pharmacogene regions

inputs.name: medication-list
inputs.desc: Patient's current and planned medications for interaction checking

outputs.name: pharmacogenomics-results
outputs.desc: Star allele calls, diplotypes, predicted phenotypes, and drug interaction table for each pharmacogene

outputs.name: prescribing-recommendations
outputs.desc: CPIC guideline-based dose adjustments or alternative drug recommendations

process: Call star alleles using Stargazer or PharmCAT for each pharmacogene. Star alleles represent defined haplotypes of functional variants (e.g., CYP2D6*4 is a splice-site variant causing no enzyme activity). Key genes: CYP2D6 (codeine, tamoxifen, many antidepressants), CYP2C19 (clopidogrel, proton pump inhibitors), CYP2C9 (warfarin, phenytoin), DPYD (fluoropyrimidines), TPMT/NUDT15 (thiopurines), UGT1A1 (irinotecan), SLCO1B1 (statins), HLA-B (abacavir, carbamazepine).

CYP2D6 requires special handling: the gene has common copy number variations (deletions: *5, duplications/multiplications: *1xN, *2xN) and hybrid alleles with CYP2D7 (e.g., *13, *36). Use read depth analysis for copy number and phasing information (or long reads) to resolve complex genotypes. An activity score system converts diplotype to phenotype: each allele gets a score (0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, or 1.5 per copy), and the sum determines metabolizer status.

Assign metabolizer phenotypes from diplotypes: poor metabolizer (PM: no functional alleles), intermediate metabolizer (IM: reduced function), normal metabolizer (NM: two functional alleles), rapid metabolizer (RM: increased function), ultrarapid metabolizer (UM: gene duplication of functional allele). Phenotype definitions are gene-specific and standardized by CPIC.

Map phenotypes to drug recommendations using CPIC guidelines. Example: CYP2D6 PM receiving codeine should avoid codeine (no conversion to morphine, lack of efficacy). CYP2C19 PM receiving clopidogrel should use alternative antiplatelet (prasugrel, ticagrelor) because clopidogrel is a prodrug requiring CYP2C19 activation. DPYD PM should avoid fluorouracil/capecitabine (risk of fatal toxicity).

For HLA-mediated adverse drug reactions: HLA-B*57:01 testing is required before abacavir (HIV treatment) to prevent hypersensitivity. HLA-B*15:02 testing before carbamazepine in Southeast Asian populations to prevent Stevens-Johnson syndrome. These are binary results (allele present/absent), not activity-score-based.

Generate the clinical report: list each tested pharmacogene with star allele result, diplotype, phenotype, associated medications, and CPIC recommendation level (A: prescribing action recommended, B: informational). Include the version of CPIC guidelines used, the genotyping/sequencing methodology, and limitations (variants not detected by the assay, genes not included in the panel).
